provenance.source: Original, hand-authored synthetic scenarios for this repository

amount_unit: integer minor currency units; no FX conversion
interpretation: These expectations test deterministic pattern matching on authored examples. The benign merchant alert is an intentional scenario-label false positive. They are not real-world precision, recall, fraud probabilities, customer risk scores, or proof of unlawful activity.

scenarios.purpose: Salary, rent, shopping and personal savings control
scenarios.analyst_context: Scripted ordinary payments; no fan-in or three-account return. Account labels describe fictitious roles, not inferred identities.

scenarios.purpose: Legitimate merchant settlement intentionally matches fan-in/pass-through
scenarios.analyst_context: Author-defined benign scenario: three customer purchases followed by an 85% payment-processor settlement. The six transaction fields cannot prove these business purposes. This expected alert is an intentional scenario-label false positive and requires external analyst context, not automatic suspicion or account blocking.

scenarios.purpose: Three-source collection followed by split rapid pass-through
scenarios.analyst_context: Scripted investigative pattern: 100000 minor units received from three sources, then 90000 (90%) sent out in two transfers within 25 minutes of the first inflow. No criminal intent or common ownership is established.

scenarios.purpose: Ordered three-account return with modest amount reduction
scenarios.analyst_context: Scripted A-to-B-to-C-to-A pattern completed in 30 minutes. Consecutive retention ratios are 95% and approximately 94.74%. Transaction links alone do not establish provenance of funds or unlawful behavior.
A mixed-currency chain must not be treated as a same-currency circle. No exchange rates or FX transactions are supplied; numerical amounts in different currencies are incomparable.

scenarios.purpose: Three-account return outside the configured 60-minute window
scenarios.analyst_context: The return arrives 70 minutes after the first transfer, outside the rule window. A negative result means only that these configured rules did not match, not that the activity is safe.

scenarios.purpose: Three senders but only 79% leaves inside the time window
scenarios.analyst_context: 79000/100000 = 79%, below the inclusive 80% threshold. The later 1000 payment occurs outside the original inflow window and must not turn the earlier interval into a match.

scenarios.purpose: Rapid high pass-through from only two distinct senders
scenarios.analyst_context: 90% leaves quickly, but only two distinct sources contribute. This is a control for the minimum-three-senders requirement.

scenarios.purpose: Ordered same-currency circle drops below the per-hop ratio
scenarios.analyst_context: The first onward transfer retains only 79% of the previous amount, so the 80-100% consecutive-hop condition fails.

scenarios.purpose: Equal timestamps do not establish ordered causality
scenarios.analyst_context: All three timestamps are equal. IDs and JSONL row order must not invent a temporal sequence.
Both onward transfers are exactly 80% of the preceding transfer and the loop completes in exactly 60 minutes. This is a scripted rule-boundary case, not evidence of a crime.

scenarios.purpose: Three senders exist only if currencies are incorrectly combined
scenarios.analyst_context: EUR has two distinct senders and USD has one; neither reaches three. Opening balances are intentionally unspecified, so observed outflow can exceed observed inflow. Never combine currencies or infer a complete account ledger from this extract.
